subject.title: [Bug]: Subagents can appear completed before the underlying delegated work is actually finished

question: Should subagent completion remain tied to child agent-run terminal lifecycle, or should explicitly completion-required child work such as background exec/process sessions block completion?
rationale: Current source intentionally separates background process follow-up from subagent liveness, so a broad fix changes runtime semantics rather than applying a small mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Add completion-required child-work contract
options.body: Introduce a narrow runtime signal for child work that must block subagent completion, with timeout, cancel, cleanup, and status coverage.

options.title: Keep terminal-run semantics
options.body: Leave subagent completion tied to agent-run terminal state and improve separate process/task visibility in status surfaces.

options.title: Block on all child processes
options.body: Hold subagent completion while any child-owned background process remains active, accepting compatibility risk for deliberately detached jobs.

recommendation.title: Add completion-required child-work contract
recommendation.body: Introduce a narrow runtime signal for child work that must block subagent completion, with timeout, cancel, cleanup, and status coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-line history points to recent ownership of the relevant subagent announce, async task wait, and background exec boundaries.
